g.passage: The bombardier beetle, a ground-dwelling insect found on every continent except Antarctica______ defends itself with a chemical spray that can reach 100°C. When threatened, the beetle mixes two stored compounds in a reinforced abdominal chamber, where enzymes trigger a rapid, heat-releasing reaction.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입되어, 여는 문장부호(쉼표)를 확인하고 닫는 문장부호를 일치시키는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 대시와 세미콜론은 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이다.
g.explanation: "a ground-dwelling insect ... Antarctica"는 주어 "The bombardier beetle"을 설명하는 비필수 동격어구이며 앞이 쉼표로 열렸으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사 "defends"를 갈라 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 대시가 동격어구를 닫을 수는 있지만 여는 부호가 쉼표이므로 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어 동격어구의 경계가 표시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a ground-dwelling insect ... Antarctica" is a nonessential appositive that describes the subject "The bombardier beetle." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, which makes A the answer. B is wrong because a semicolon would split the subject from its verb "defends," and the part before the semicolon isn't an independent clause. C is wrong because a dash can close an appositive, but only when a dash opened it, and here a comma did. D is wrong because without any closing punctuation, nothing marks where the appositive ends.

g.passage: Written in spare contemporary prose but steeped in the gaslit gloom of a Victorian novel, Mara Ellison's The Lamplighter's Daughter unfolds through a single recollecting voice. The novel's narrator, a retired schoolmistress who never left the fen village where she was born______ recalls the bitter winter when the village lost its only physician and the roads vanished beneath the snow.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'a retired schoolmistress ... was born'은 주어 narrator를 설명하는 비필수 동격 구이고, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어 narrator와 동사 recalls가 바르게 연결된다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어+동격 구에 불과하므로 쓸 수 없다. C의 대시는 동격 구를 닫을 수는 있지만, 여는 부호가 쉼표이므로 짝이 맞지 않는다. D처럼 부호를 생략하면 동격 구가 열리기만 하고 닫히지 않아, born recalls처럼 동사가 엉뚱하게 이어지는 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a retired schoolmistress ... was born" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "narrator." Because a comma opens it, a comma must also close it so that the subject "narrator" connects properly to its verb "recalls." That makes B correct. A is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and the text before the blank is only a subject plus an appositive, with no main verb. C is wrong because a dash can close an appositive, but it doesn't pair with the opening comma. D is wrong because without punctuation the appositive is opened but never closed, so "was born recalls" runs together awkwardly.
g.design: 빈칸 직전의 긴 관계절('who never left ... was born') 때문에 훑어 읽으면 절 끝에서 세미콜론/대시/무부호를 고르기 쉽지만, 정답을 고르려면 동격 구가 쉼표로 열렸다는 점과 주어-동사 연결이라는 두 가지를 함께 따져야 한다.

g.passage: Along the coast of northern Chile, scattered pockets of vegetation known as lomas—"fog oases" in the Atacama Desert—survive on the camanchaca, a dense marine fog that drifts inland during the winter months______ the cacti, shrubs, and lichens of these oases would receive almost no water at all.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'scattered pockets ... survive on the camanchaca, a dense marine fog ... months'는 동격구로 끝나는 독립절이고, 'without it'으로 시작하는 뒷부분도 주어(the cacti...)와 동사(would receive)를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있고, 도입 전치사구 'without it' 뒤에는 쉼표가 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 지문에 이미 대시 한 쌍(lomas—...—)이 쓰였는데 대시를 하나 더 써서 문장 구조를 흐리고, 도입구 뒤 쉼표도 빠져 있다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "scattered pockets ... survive on the camanchaca, a dense marine fog ... months," is an independent clause that ends with an appositive. The part starting with "without it" is also an independent clause, since it has its own subject ("the cacti, shrubs, and lichens") and verb ("would receive"). You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, and the introductory phrase "without it" needs a comma after it, so C is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B adds another dash to a sentence that already uses a pair of dashes, which muddles the sentence's structure, and it leaves out the comma after the introductory phrase. D joins the two independent clauses with no punctuation, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: The long appositive at the end of the first clause hides where that clause ends. Students who skim may read "without it" as a modifier attached to the appositive and pick the comma in A. Choices B and D distract with the dash already used in the sentence and with a run-on.

g.passage: When engineers at a Dutch firm designed a floating solar farm for a reservoir near Utrecht, they faced an unusual problem. The panels, mounted on buoyant plastic pontoons that drift slightly with the wind, could not be anchored rigidly to the reservoir ______ the team developed flexible mooring lines that stretch and recoil, allowing the array to shift without tearing loose.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "The panels ... could not be anchored rigidly to the reservoir floor"와 뒤의 "the team developed ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 'mounted on ... wind'라는 긴 삽입 수식어 때문에 주절이 길어 보이지만, 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하고 접속부사 instead 뒤에는 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 접속부사를 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 절 경계는 맞지만 문장 앞의 접속부사 instead 뒤에 쉼표가 빠졌다. D는 경계 부호가 없어 instead가 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 읽히며 두 독립절이 쉼표 하나로만 이어진다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, "The panels ... could not be anchored rigidly to the reservoir floor" is an independent clause, and so is "the team developed flexible mooring lines..." after it. The long modifier "mounted on ... wind" makes the first clause look complicated, but it is still a complete clause. Two independent clauses can be joined by a semicolon, and the conjunctive adverb "instead" that starts the second clause should be followed by a comma, so A is correct. B links the clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. C gets the boundary right but leaves out the comma after the introductory "instead." D puts no punctuation between the clauses, so "instead" seems attached to the first clause and the two clauses are joined by a comma alone.
g.design: 긴 비필수 분사구 삽입으로 주절 경계 파악을 어렵게 하고, 세미콜론 유무와 접속부사 뒤 쉼표라는 두 판단을 결합했다.

g.passage: The glasswing butterfly (Greta oto), a Central American species whose wings are almost entirely transparent, has long puzzled biologists. Studying the wings under an electron microscope, a research team found that irregular nanoscale pillars covering the wing membrane, rather than the sparse bristle-like scales scattered across it, cause the surface to reflect very little ______ this property may help the butterfly escape predators by making it nearly invisible as it flies through the forest understory.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 문장에 'rather than...' 삽입구와 긴 주어가 있어 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했고, 빈칸 뒤가 독립절임을 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단을 요구한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'a research team found that ... reflect very little light'와 빈칸 뒤 'this property may help the butterfly escape predators ...'는 둘 다 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 관계대명사 which를 넣었지만 뒤의 절에 which가 들어갈 빈자리가 없어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, "a research team found that ... cause the surface to reflect very little light" is a complete independent clause, and after the blank, "this property may help the butterfly escape predators ..." is also an independent clause. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D adds the relative pronoun "which," but the clause that follows is already complete, so "which" has no role to play and the sentence is ungrammatical.

g.passage: In the novelist's latest work, a modern story told in the manner of a Victorian melodrama, the opening chapter turns on a single moment. The housekeeper, a widow who had served the Ashcombe family for nearly three decades and who knew every creak of the old house's staircases, paused outside the library door______ inside, by the light of a single guttering candle, the master of the house was feeding his late wife's letters, one by one, into the fire.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구를 걷어 내면 앞부분은 "The housekeeper ... paused outside the library door"라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "inside, ... the master of the house was feeding ... letters"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D의 "which"는 관계절을 만들지만 뒤에 이미 주어 "the master"가 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않으므로 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive about the widow, the first part reads "The housekeeper ... paused outside the library door," which is an independent clause. The part after the blank, "inside, ... the master of the house was feeding ... letters," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "which," but the following clause already has its own subject, "the master," so the relative clause doesn't work and the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: 긴 동격구와 빈칸 뒤 삽입구 때문에 두 독립절이라는 구조가 잘 보이지 않게 했다. 그래서 주절의 핵심 구조를 다시 찾은 뒤 절의 경계를 판단해야 풀 수 있다.

g.passage: Along the coast of northern Chile and southern Peru, the fog oases of the Atacama Desert—isolated patches of grasses, cacti, and flowering shrubs that locals call lomas and that survive almost entirely on moisture drawn from coastal mist______ can expand dramatically in years when El Niño conditions thicken the offshore fog bank.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "the fog oases of the Atacama Desert" 뒤에서 대시로 시작한 삽입 동격어구는 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤 동사 "can expand"가 주어 "fog oases"와 바로 이어져야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표로 대시를 닫을 수 없고, 주어가 아직 동사를 갖지 못했는데 "and they"가 새 절을 연결해 문장이 불완전해진다. B는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 단편이고 대시도 닫히지 않는다. C는 대시와 쉼표의 짝이 맞지 않고, 주어를 "they"로 불필요하게 반복한다.
g.explanation_en: The dash after "the fog oases of the Atacama Desert" opens an appositive interruption, so it has to be closed with a matching dash. After that, the verb "can expand" connects straight back to the subject "fog oases." That makes D correct. A is wrong because a comma can't close a dash, and "and they" starts a new clause even though the main subject still has no verb. B leaves everything before the semicolon as a fragment with no verb, and the dash is never closed. C mismatches the dash with a comma and repeats the subject unnecessarily with "they."
g.design: 긴 대시 삽입구 때문에 주어와 동사가 멀리 떨어져 있다. 학생은 대시의 짝을 맞추는 규칙을 적용하고, 동시에 주절이 아직 동사를 기다리고 있다는 점도 확인해야 한다. 오답 3개는 모두 그럴듯한 절 연결 방식을 제시한다.

g.passage: In the decades after 1850, the spread of public lending libraries changed how working people in British industrial towns spent their evenings. Manchester's Free Library, which opened in 1852 with a collection drawn largely from donated volumes, quickly attracted mill ______ many of them had never before been able to borrow a book without paying a subscription fee.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Manchester's Free Library ... quickly attracted mill workers'는 긴 비필수 삽입절을 지나 완성된 독립절이고, 뒤의 'many of them had never ... fee'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하고, 접속부사 indeed는 두 번째 절 앞에 두고 쉼표를 붙이는 A가 옳다. B와 D는 쉼표와 접속부사만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 세미콜론 위치는 맞아 보이지만 indeed를 첫 절 끝에 붙여 의미상 '정말로 노동자들을 끌어들였다'처럼 어색해지고, 뒤 절과의 강조 관계가 사라지며 관례적인 접속부사 위치에도 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Manchester's Free Library ... quickly attracted mill workers," is a complete independent clause once you skip past the long nonessential clause in the middle. What follows, "many of them had never ... fee," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and the transition "indeed" belongs at the start of the second clause, followed by a comma, so A is correct. B and D join the two clauses with only a comma and a transition, which creates a comma splice. C does put a semicolon between the clauses, but it attaches "indeed" to the end of the first clause, so the word no longer introduces the second clause as the stronger point, and that placement breaks the usual way a transition is used.
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 절의 경계가 잘 안 보이게 했다. 그 결과 독립절 판단과 접속부사 위치 판단, 두 단계를 거쳐야 답이 나온다.

g.passage: The Falkirk Wheel, a rotating boat lift in Scotland that joins two canals whose water levels differ by about 24 meters, and the only structure of its kind in the world______ needs only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours of electricity to complete each half turn, because the two water-filled gondolas it carries always balance each other.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 'The Falkirk Wheel' 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 동격 삽입구는 'meters,' 뒤의 'and the only structure ... world'까지 이어지므로, 빈칸에서 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 'needs'가 연결된다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞에 독립절이 없으므로 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓는다. C의 대시는 삽입구를 시작한 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 'and it'을 넣어 주어 'The Falkirk Wheel'에 동사가 없는 불완전한 문장을 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The appositive that starts after "The Falkirk Wheel," keeps going past "meters," and includes "and the only structure of its kind in the world." You need to close it with a comma so the subject can connect to the verb "needs." That makes B correct. A is wrong because a semicolon needs a complete independent clause on both sides, and here it would cut the subject off from its verb. C is wrong because the appositive opened with a comma, so a closing dash doesn't match it. D is wrong because adding "and it" leaves "The Falkirk Wheel" without a verb of its own.
g.design: The appositive contains its own internal comma and an "and" phrase, so a quick reader may think it has already ended. The student has to see where the appositive really stops and then match the opening punctuation.

g.passage: Off the coast of Portugal, marine biologist Ana Ferreira has documented an unusual partnership in shallow kelp forests. The decorator crab Pisa armata, a slow-moving species that divers often overlook, attaches living sponges to its shell for camouflage______ the sponges gain access to food particles that the crab stirs up as it walks across the seafloor.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The decorator crab ... attaches living sponges to its shell for camouflage"와 뒤 "the sponges gain access ..."는 각각 완전한 독립절이므로, 두 절 사이에는 세미콜론과 같은 강한 경계가 필요하다. 접속부사구 "in turn"은 두 번째 절을 이끌며, 세미콜론 뒤에 오고 그 뒤에는 쉼표가 붙어야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 "in turn" 뒤 쉼표가 빠졌다. D는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The decorator crab ... attaches living sponges to its shell for camouflage," and the text after it, "the sponges gain access ...," are both independent clauses, so they need a strong boundary such as a semicolon. The transitional phrase "in turn" starts the second clause, so it goes after the semicolon and should be followed by a comma, which makes C correct. A joins two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. B has the right semicolon but leaves out the comma after "in turn." D puts no boundary punctuation between the two clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤에서 주절의 끝을 찾아 절 경계를 판단해야 하고, 접속부사구의 구두점까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단 문항이다. A와 B는 각각 일부만 맞는 함정이다.

g.passage: In Mara Ellery's novel The Lantern House, set in a present-day coastal town but told with the brooding atmosphere of a Victorian novel, the narrator's aunt Theodora—a widow who keeps every letter she has ever received, sorted by year, in a lacquered box beneath her bed______ refuses to open the one that arrives on the morning of the first autumn fog.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'a widow who keeps ... beneath her bed'는 주어 Theodora를 설명하는 비필수 동격 삽입구이며, 앞에서 대시로 시작했으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 주어 Theodora와 동사 refuses가 연결된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 ', and'를 넣어 refuses를 삽입구 속 동사 keeps와 병렬로 만들어, 주절의 주어 Theodora에 대응하는 본동사가 없어진다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 필요하지만 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어+삽입구일 뿐이고, 뒷부분도 주어가 없다. C의 쉼표는 삽입구 안에 이미 쉼표가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫는 것은 부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a widow who keeps ... beneath her bed" is a nonessential appositive that describes the subject, Theodora. Because it opens with a dash, it has to close with a dash too, which lets the subject "Theodora" connect to its verb "refuses." That makes D correct. A adds ", and," which makes "refuses" parallel with "keeps" inside the appositive, so the main clause is left without a verb for Theodora. B uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on each side, but the text before the blank is only a subject plus an interrupting phrase, and the text after it has no subject. C may look right because the appositive already contains commas, but an interruption that opens with a dash can't be closed with a comma, since the punctuation has to match.
g.design: The opening dash sits far before the blank, and an internal comma ("sorted by year,") makes a closing comma tempting. To answer, the student has to find the subject–verb link and then match the dash pair.

g.passage: Rain that falls on the Angolan highlands between November and March does not reach Botswana's Okavango Delta until months later. That water, which must cross hundreds of kilometers of nearly flat terrain before arriving in ______ moves so slowly that the delta's peak flood coincides with the region's dry season.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: A long nonessential clause sits between the subject "That water" and the verb "moves." Students have to spot the opening comma, close the clause with a matching comma, and see that a semicolon or added subject would break apart the single main clause.
g.explanation: 주절의 주어 "That water"와 동사 "moves" 사이에 비필수 관계절 "which must cross ... arriving in Botswana"가 끼어 있으므로, 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이어야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어+관계절에 불과하므로 틀리다. C는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입절의 경계가 흐려진다. D는 주어 it을 덧붙여 "That water"를 동사 없는 주어로 남기므로 문법에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "That water" is separated from its verb "moves" by the nonessential clause "which must cross ... arriving in Botswana." That clause opens with a comma, so it needs a matching comma to close it, which makes A correct. B is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and the part before it is only a subject plus a relative clause, with no main verb. C leaves out the closing comma, so the interrupting clause has no clear end. D adds the subject "it," which leaves "That water" as a subject with no verb.

g.passage: The Public Libraries Act of 1850, which allowed British towns to collect a small local tax to pay for free lending libraries, at first had little practical effect ______ more than 300 municipalities had adopted it, opening reading rooms to working-class residents who had previously had almost no access to books.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The Public Libraries Act ... had little practical effect"는 긴 비필수 관계절이 끼어 있지만 그 자체로 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "more than 300 municipalities had adopted it"도 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절은 세미콜론으로 구분하고, 도입 전치사구 "by 1900" 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 쉼표+and로 절을 연결한 점은 맞지만, 도입구 "by 1900"을 닫는 쉼표가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Even with the long nonessential clause in the middle, "The Public Libraries Act ... had little practical effect" is a complete independent clause, and "more than 300 municipalities had adopted it" is another one. Two independent clauses can be separated by a semicolon, and the introductory phrase "by 1900" should be followed by a comma, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D is right to join the clauses with a comma and "and," but it leaves out the comma that should close the introductory phrase "by 1900."
g.design: The long nonessential relative clause hides where the main clause ends. D is correct about the clause boundary but wrong about the punctuation after the introductory phrase, so students have to check both judgments together.

g.passage: In 1978, structural engineer William LeMessurier, the designer of New York's fifty-nine-story Citicorp Center, realized that the tower's diagonal braces, which had been bolted rather than welded to save money, might fail under strong winds striking the building at an angle______ crews quietly worked at night to weld heavy steel plates over more than two hundred of the bolted joints.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구와 비필수 관계절을 포함하지만 결국 'LeMessurier ... realized that ...'라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'crews quietly worked ...'도 독립절이다. C는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 연결하고, 도입 부사구 'over the following weeks' 뒤에 쉼표를 둬 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결한 콤마 스플라이스이다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종결 문장(run-on)이다. D는 콜론 뒤에 독립절이 오긴 하지만 도입구와 주절 사이에 세미콜론을 넣어 'over the following weeks'를 완전한 절처럼 잘못 분리한다.
g.explanation_en: Even though the text before the blank includes a long appositive and a nonessential clause, at its core it's an independent clause ("LeMessurier ... realized that ..."), and "crews quietly worked ..." after the blank is also an independent clause. C works because it joins the two clauses with a semicolon and puts a comma after the introductory phrase "over the following weeks." A uses only commas to join two independent clauses, so it's a comma splice. B joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D is wrong because the colon is fine, but the semicolon splits the introductory phrase off from its main clause as if the phrase were a complete clause.
g.design: 긴 동격구와 관계절 때문에 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 오답 A·D는 쉼표와 콜론을 부분적으로 맞게 쓰고 있어서 정답과 꼼꼼히 비교해야만 걸러진다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: Biologist Ana Ruiz has spent a decade tracking the bluehead wrasse, a small reef fish whose largest females can change sex when a dominant male disappears from the group. In her most recent field season off the coast of Panama, Ruiz removed males from several reefs and timed the response of the remaining fish. The results surprised ______ the transforming females began displaying male courtship behavior within minutes, long before any changes to their reproductive organs had occurred.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 'The results surprised her'와 뒤 'the transforming females ... occurred'가 모두 독립절이라는 점을 확인하고, 뒤 절이 앞 절의 '놀라운 결과'를 구체화한다는 문맥까지 연결해야 한다. 쉼표만 쓴 A(쉼표 연결 오류), 문장부호 없는 C(무종지문)를 배제하고, 문법적으로는 가능해 보이는 B를 의미 관계로 배제하게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The results surprised her"와 빈칸 뒤 "the transforming females began displaying..."은 각각 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤 절은 결과가 무엇이었기에 놀라웠는지를 구체적으로 설명한다. 콜론은 독립절 뒤에 그 내용을 풀어 설명하는 요소를 이어 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. B는 쉼표+and로 문법상 연결은 되지만, 뒤 절을 놀라움과 별개로 덧붙인 사건처럼 만들어 그 절이 놀라움의 내용이라는 관계를 흐린다. 따라서 이 문맥에서는 콜론이 가장 적절하다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("The results surprised her") and the text after it ("the transforming females began displaying...") are both independent clauses, and the second one explains exactly what was surprising. A colon is used after an independent clause to introduce an explanation of it, so D is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, which makes a run-on sentence. B is grammatically possible with a comma plus "and," but it makes the second clause sound like a separate event added on, not the reason for the surprise. That hides the explaining relationship, so the colon in D fits this context best.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

g.passage: In Mara Ellisford's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the widowed bookkeeper Agnes Thorne keeps two sets of accounts for the failing textile mill where she works: one for the owners, who demand reassuring figures, and one for herself, in which every lost shilling is recorded with grim precision. Late in the book, after a fire destroys the mill's warehouse, Agnes faces a choice that the reader has long anticipated ______ she can surrender the honest ledger to the magistrate or burn it alongside the ruined stock.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Agnes faces a choice that the reader has long anticipated'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'she can surrender ... or burn it ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며 그 '선택'의 내용을 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절을 설명하는 독립절을 이어 주는 콜론을 쓴 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 쉼표+and로 문법적 연결은 가능해 보이지만, 뒤 절이 새로 추가되는 정보가 아니라 'choice'의 내용 자체이므로 설명 관계가 사라져 논리가 어색하다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Agnes faces a choice that the reader has long anticipated," is an independent clause, and the text after it, "she can surrender ... or burn it ...," is also an independent clause that spells out what that choice is. A colon is the right way to introduce a clause that explains the one before it, so A is correct. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C looks grammatical, but "and" treats the second clause as an added event rather than the content of the choice, so the explanatory link is lost. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation, creating a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 관계절 수식어(that the reader has long anticipated) 뒤에서 절 경계를 판단하게 해 'anticipated' 뒤 독립절을 수식어 연장으로 오독하기 쉽게 했다. 쉼표+and 오답을 그럴듯하게 두어 의미 관계까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

g.passage: Botswana's Okavango Delta reaches its greatest extent in the middle of the dry season, a timing that puzzles many visitors. The explanation lies far upstream. Rain falling on the Angolan highlands, more than 1,000 kilometers to the northwest, needs roughly four months to creep across the flat Kalahari basin to the ______ by the time the floodwater finally spreads across the delta's channels and islands, local rains have long since ended.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 문장 앞부분에 삽입구(more than 1,000 kilometers...)와 긴 전치사구가 있고 뒤 절이 'by the time ...'이라는 종속 구로 시작해, 두 번째 독립절의 시작 위치를 헷갈리게 만들었다. 오답은 쉼표 연결 오류, 무구두점 연결, 쉼표 없는 등위접속사로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Rain ... needs roughly four months ... to the delta'는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'by the time ... local rains have long since ended'도 'by the time' 구 다음에 주어 local rains와 동사 have ended를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 정답은 B이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 구두점 없이 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 되고, 'by the time'이 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 잘못 읽히게 된다. D는 등위접속사 so를 썼지만 두 독립절 사이에 필요한 쉼표가 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Rain ... needs roughly four months ... to the delta," is an independent clause. The text after it, "by the time ... local rains have long since ended," is also an independent clause: once you get past the introductory "by the time" phrase, it has its own subject (local rains) and verb (have ended). A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so B is the answer. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence and wrongly makes "by the time" look like it modifies the first clause. D uses the coordinating conjunction "so" but leaves out the comma that must come before it when it joins two independent clauses.

g.passage: In the 1840s, the British engineer Edwin Chadwick argued that disease in crowded industrial towns spread mainly through filth and poor drainage. His 1842 report on the sanitary condition of the laboring population, which drew on testimony from doctors and local officials across the country, ______ it helped persuade Parliament to pass the Public Health Act of 1848, one of the first laws to give towns authority over sewers and water supplies.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 비제한적 관계절이 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓아 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 쉼표+and 오답은 문법적으로 거의 맞아 보이지만 쉼표 배치가 틀려 있어 비교해야 배제된다.
g.explanation: 주어 'His 1842 report'의 동사는 삽입된 관계절 뒤에 오는 'was widely read'이고, 그 뒤에 'it helped persuade…'라는 또 하나의 독립절이 이어진다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 정답은 C이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 쉼표+and 조합이라 맞아 보이지만, 이 짧은 두 절에서는 쉼표가 and 앞에 와야 하며 여기서는 'read, and'로 실제로 맞는 형태처럼 보인다는 점에 주의해야 한다. 그러나 B는 앞 관계절이 쉼표로 닫힌 뒤 동사와 접속사가 결합되어 'which … country, was widely read, and it'에서 문제는 없지만, D는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "His 1842 report" finds its verb, "was widely read," only after the long nonrestrictive clause that interrupts it. After that verb comes a second independent clause, "it helped persuade Parliament…," so the two clauses have to be joined correctly. C uses a semicolon, which is a standard way to join two independent clauses. A joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D puts no punctuation between them at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

g.passage: To cut drag on cargo ships, engineers at a Danish shipyard tested a hull coating modeled on shark skin, whose tiny ridged scales disrupt the turbulent flow of water along a moving surface. The results of the eighteen-month trial, which tracked fuel consumption on identical shipping routes, were ______ treated vessels burned roughly 6 percent less fuel than untreated ones.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 삽입된 관계절(which ... routes)을 걷어내면 주절은 "The results ... were striking"이고, 뒤에 "treated vessels burned ..."라는 또 하나의 독립절이 온다. 뒤 절이 '놀라운 결과'의 구체적 내용을 설명하므로 콜론으로 잇는 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 because로 시작하는 종속절만 남아 불완전한 문장이 되고, 의미상으로도 인과관계가 맞지 않는다. C는 문장부호 없이 and만으로 두 독립절을 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 되고, 설명 관계도 드러내지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the inserted clause (which ... routes), the main clause is "The results ... were striking," and it's followed by a second independent clause, "treated vessels burned ...". That second clause spells out what made the results striking, so a colon is the right link, which makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. B puts "because" after a semicolon, which leaves only a dependent clause on that side, and it also suggests a cause-and-effect relationship that isn't there. C joins two independent clauses with "and" but no comma, so it's a run-on, and it doesn't show that the second clause explains the first.
g.design: A long relative clause separates the subject from "were striking," so students have to find the real main clause before seeing that two independent clauses meet at the blank. Each wrong answer is partly reasonable: one uses a comma, one uses a semicolon, and one uses a conjunction.

g.passage: Biologist Lena Ostrova studied a population of sea slugs in a tidal lagoon off the coast of Portugal, tracking how individuals responded to rising water temperatures over three summers. The slugs, which steal functioning chloroplasts from the algae they ______ during heat waves, the slugs relied far more heavily on this stolen photosynthesis than on feeding.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: eat, can survive for weeks without food;
eat can survive for weeks without food,
eat, can survive for weeks without food,
eat; can survive for weeks without food;
g.design: 비필수 관계절을 닫는 쉼표와 이어지는 두 독립절 사이의 경계를 동시에 판단하게 해, 한 경계만 맞힌 오답(B, C)과 둘 다 틀린 오답(D)을 구성했다.
g.explanation: A가 정답이다. 비필수 관계절 "which steal ... they eat"는 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 이후 "The slugs ... can survive for weeks without food"와 "during heat waves, the slugs relied..."는 각각 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 연결해야 한다. B는 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 없고, 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 관계절은 올바르게 닫았지만 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 연결해 콤마 스플라이스가 생긴다. D는 주어 "The slugs"와 동사 "can survive" 사이에 세미콜론을 넣어 앞부분이 완전한 절이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. The nonessential clause "which steal ... they eat" opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too. After that, "The slugs ... can survive for weeks without food" and "during heat waves, the slugs relied..." are both independent clauses, so a semicolon should join them. B leaves out the comma that closes the nonessential clause, and it joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C closes the nonessential clause correctly, but it still joins the two independent clauses with just a comma, so it's also a comma splice. g.passage: The narrator of Imogen Varga's novel The Salt Ledger, a widowed lighthouse keeper who records every passing ship in a leather-bound book, rarely speaks directly of her own grief______ she lets the entries themselves, terse and increasingly irregular, reveal how loss has unsettled her once orderly life.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a widowed lighthouse keeper ... book)를 지나면 주어 The narrator와 동사 speaks로 된 독립절이 grief에서 끝나고, she lets ...로 두 번째 독립절이 시작된다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하고 접속부사 instead 뒤에는 쉼표를 두어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 세미콜론을 instead 뒤에 두어, instead가 앞 절에 붙고 두 절은 여전히 쉼표로만 이어져 의미와 구조가 모두 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Once you look past the long appositive (a widowed lighthouse keeper ... book), you can see that "The narrator ... rarely speaks directly of her own grief" is a complete independent clause. "She lets the entries ... reveal..." starts a second independent clause. Two independent clauses joined by the transition "instead" need a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so B is correct. A joins the clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice, and C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on. g.passage: The Flow Country of northern Scotland, a sweeping expanse of waterlogged blanket bog that took thousands of years to form, holds more carbon in its peat than all of the United Kingdom's forests combined______ draining even small patches of the bog for farming or tree planting can release large amounts of that stored carbon into the atmosphere.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 때문에 주절 경계가 흐려지도록 하고, 접속부사 'consequently'를 쉼표로만 연결하는 그럴듯한 오답을 넣어 절 경계 규칙과 접속부사 규칙을 둘 다 판단하게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'The Flow Country ... holds more carbon ... combined'는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 'draining ... can release ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하고, 'consequently' 같은 접속부사는 그 뒤에 쉼표를 붙여 쓰므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 'consequently'를 넣었지만 접속부사는 등위접속사가 아니므로 쉼표만으로는 두 절을 이을 수 없다. D는 첫 절 뒤에 문장부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("The Flow Country ... holds more carbon ... combined") form an independent clause, and the words after it ("draining ... can release ...") form another independent clause with its own subject and verb. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B adds "consequently," but a conjunctive adverb isn't a coordinating conjunction, so a comma alone still can't join the clauses. D puts no punctuation after the first clause, which makes it a run-on sentence.

g.passage: Britain's Public Libraries Act of 1850 allowed towns to fund free libraries through local taxes, a significant shift at a time when most books were too costly for working families. One of the law's most vocal supporters in Parliament, Joseph Brotherton, a Salford manufacturer who had himself labored in a cotton mill as a child______ argued that libraries would give workers a constructive alternative to the alehouse.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 'One of the law's most vocal supporters'와 동사 'argued' 사이에 동격 삽입구 'Joseph Brotherton, a Salford manufacturer ... as a child'가 들어 있다. 삽입구는 앞의 쉼표로 시작했으므로 끝에도 쉼표가 와야 하며, 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론과 B의 콜론은 앞에 완전한 독립절이 있어야 쓸 수 있는데, 빈칸 앞에는 주어만 있고 동사가 없으므로 둘 다 틀리다. C의 ', and'는 'argued'를 'labored'와 나란히 놓인 두 번째 동작처럼 만들어 주절에 동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "One of the law's most vocal supporters" is separated from its verb "argued" by the appositive phrase "Joseph Brotherton, a Salford manufacturer ... as a child." That appositive opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too. This makes D correct. A semicolon (A) or a colon (B) has to come after a complete independent clause, but the words before the blank are only a subject with no verb of their own. Choice C, ", and," makes "argued" look like a second action paired with "labored," which leaves the main clause without a verb.
g.design: The blank is placed after a long appositive with an embedded relative clause, so a quick reader might think a clause has already ended. Students must first find the subject and verb (two steps) and then close the appositive with a matching comma. ", and" is a tempting trap because it seems to join two actions.

g.passage: The MX3D Bridge, a 12-meter stainless steel footbridge built by robotic arms that deposited molten metal layer by layer, was installed over an Amsterdam canal in 2021. Before the bridge opened to pedestrians, engineers fitted its frame with a network of small sensors______ these devices continuously measured strain, vibration, and temperature, allowing researchers to model how the printed metal behaved under real foot traffic.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'engineers fitted ... sensors'와 뒤 'these devices continuously measured ...'는 각각 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하다. A는 세미콜론으로 두 절을 나누고, 뒤 절의 도입 수식어 'in operation' 다음에 쉼표를 찍어 올바르다. B는 'in operation'을 쉼표 두 개로 감싸 삽입구처럼 보여 맞는 듯하지만, 결국 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 콤마 스플라이스다. C는 두 절 사이에 문장부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D 역시 쉼표만으로 절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스이며, 도입구 뒤 쉼표도 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("engineers fitted ... sensors") and the words after it ("these devices continuously measured ...") are both independent clauses, so you need a strong boundary, such as a semicolon, between them. A works because the semicolon separates the two clauses and the comma after "in operation" sets off the introductory phrase of the second clause. B looks tempting because it wraps "in operation" in a pair of commas, but that still joins two independent clauses with only commas, which is a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. D is also a comma splice, and it leaves out the comma after the introductory phrase too.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격구와 수식어를 넣어 절의 경계가 잘 보이지 않게 했습니다. 또 도입구 'in operation'을 쉼표로 감싼 오답을 넣어, 독립절 두 개를 알아보고 쉼표 위치까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하도록 설계했습니다.

g.passage: In a study of mental accounting, economist Rafaela Okonjo surveyed 1,400 households about how they used windfalls such as tax refunds and work bonuses. She found that the tendency of consumers with irregular monthly incomes to treat a refund as "found money," spending it more freely than an equal amount of regular wages, ______ much stronger than the same tendency among salaried workers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "She found that" 뒤 that절의 주어는 단수 명사 "the tendency"이고, 긴 수식어구 "of consumers ... regular wages" 뒤에 이 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. 또 주절 동사 "found"가 과거이므로 단수 과거형 B "was"가 정답이다. A "were"는 시제는 맞지만 가까이 있는 복수 명사 "consumers"나 "wages"에 수를 맞춘 것이어서 단수 주어 "tendency"와 일치하지 않는다. C "being"은 분사여서 that절에 정동사가 없게 된다. D "have been"은 복수형이라 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the that-clause after "She found that" is the singular noun "the tendency." After the long modifier "of consumers ... regular wages," the clause still needs a main verb that agrees with that subject. The main verb "found" is in the past tense, so the singular past-tense verb in B, "was," is correct. A, "were," has the right tense, but it agrees with nearby plural nouns like "consumers" or "wages" instead of the singular subject "tendency." C, "being," is a participle, so the that-clause would be left without a main verb. D, "have been," is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject.

g.passage: In Kuşköy, a village in northeastern Turkey, farmers once communicated across steep valleys by whistling entire Turkish sentences. In 2015, the recordings of whistled speech that biopsychologist Onur Güntürkün's team gathered from villagers fluent in the practice ______ that, unlike ordinary spoken language, whistled language is processed substantially by both hemispheres of the brain.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 관계절(that...practice) 뒤 복수 주어 recordings와의 수 일치를 먼저 판단하고, 'In 2015'라는 문맥으로 시제를 확인하는 두 단계 구조. 단수형 오답은 가까운 명사 speech/team/practice에 끌리도록 설계.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the recordings'(복수)이고, 'of whistled speech that ... in the practice'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 맞는 정동사가 필요하고, 'In 2015'가 과거의 특정 시점을 나타내므로 과거형 C(revealed)가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이지만 가까이 있는 단수 명사(practice, team)에 맞춘 단수형이라 복수 주어 recordings와 일치하지 않으며, D의 현재완료는 특정 과거 시점 'In 2015'와도 함께 쓸 수 없다. B는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the recordings," which is plural. Everything from "of whistled speech" to "in the practice" is a long modifier describing that subject. So the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a plural subject, and because "In 2015" points to a specific past time, the past-tense verb in C ("revealed") is correct. A and D are main verbs, but they're singular forms that match nearby singular nouns like "practice" or "team" instead of the plural "recordings." D's present perfect also can't be used with a specific past time like "In 2015." B is a participle, so it would leave the sentence with no main verb, and the sentence wouldn't be complete.

g.passage: Textile artist Anni Albers, whose woven wall hangings drew on Andean weaving techniques that she had studied for decades in museum collections and books, ______ her ideas about the structure of cloth in the 1965 book On Weaving, which is still read by designers today.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'Anni Albers'이고, 그 뒤의 whose절은 삽입된 수식어이다. 그 수식어 안에는 이미 동사 'drew'와 'had studied'가 있지만, 그 동사들은 주절의 동사가 아니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 주절의 정동사가 필요하며, 과거형 정동사인 A 'set out'이 정답이다. B는 현재분사, C는 완료분사, D는 to부정사여서 모두 문장에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Anni Albers," and the whose clause after it is an inserted modifier. That modifier already contains the verbs "drew" and "had studied," but those verbs aren't the main verb of the sentence. So the blank needs a finite main verb, and choice A, the past tense "set out," is correct. Choice B is a present participle, choice C is a perfect participle, and choice D is an infinitive, so each one leaves the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 whose절 수식어 안의 동사 때문에 주절 동사가 이미 있는 것처럼 착각하게 해서, 정동사와 비정동사를 구별하는 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

g.passage: Astronomers studying the nearby star cluster Messier 67 have long been puzzled by its "blue stragglers," stars that appear hotter and younger than their neighbors. A team led by astrophysicist Aaron Geller proposed that many of these stars gained mass from close companions. The orbits of the binary systems in which blue stragglers are most often found, according to Geller's simulations, ______ the long, nearly circular paths expected if one star had slowly siphoned gas from the other.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 주어 'The orbits'와 동사 사이에 단수 명사(systems/stragglers는 복수이지만 Geller's simulations, 단수 'binary' 느낌)와 삽입구를 넣어 일치 판단과 정동사 필요성을 함께 판단하게 했다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The orbits'이고, 그 뒤의 'of the binary systems in which ... are most often found'와 삽입구 'according to Geller's simulations'는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 복수 정동사가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이어서 복수 주어 'orbits'와 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The orbits." Everything between it and the blank ("of the binary systems in which ... are most often found" and the aside "according to Geller's simulations") just modifies it. So the sentence needs a plural finite verb, which makes B correct. A and D are finite verbs, but they're singular, so they don't agree with the plural subject "orbits." C is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb, so it wouldn't be a complete sentence.

g.passage: In a 2019 field study of ride-share drivers, economists tested whether workers set daily income targets and quit once they reach them. The data, drawn from thousands of shifts logged across several mid-sized cities, ______ that drivers were more likely to end a shift after crossing a round-number earnings threshold, even when demand and fares remained high.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The data"이고, 그 뒤의 "drawn from ... cities"는 주어를 수식하는 분사구일 뿐 동사가 아니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 문장의 정동사가 필요하며, 앞 문장의 과거 시제(tested)와도 맞는 C "revealed"가 정답이다. A "revealing"과 D "having revealed"는 분사여서 정동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다. "drawn"을 동사로 착각하면 A나 D가 맞아 보일 수 있다. B "to reveal"은 부정사여서 역시 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장을 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The data," and "drawn from ... cities" is a participial phrase that modifies the subject. It is not the main verb. That means the blank needs a finite main verb, and C, "revealed," supplies one in the past tense, which also matches "tested" in the previous sentence. A ("revealing") and D ("having revealed") are participles, so they can't serve as the main verb, and the sentence would stay incomplete. They may look right if you mistake "drawn" for the verb. B ("to reveal") is an infinitive, so it also leaves the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 분사 수식어(drawn from...)가 주어와 빈칸 사이에 끼어 있어 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 구분을 위해 문장 구조 파악이 필요하도록 설계했다. 오답 A·D는 drawn을 동사로 오인하면 그럴듯해 보인다.

g.passage: In the mountain villages of northeastern Turkey, some residents still communicate across valleys using a whistled form of Turkish. The collection of recordings that researchers made of these whistlers, many of them shepherds who learned the practice as children, ______ how speakers preserve distinctions between vowels by shifting pitch alone.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The collection'이고, 'of recordings ... as children'은 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 현재 시제이지만 빈칸 가까이에 있는 복수 명사 'recordings'나 'whistlers', 'shepherds'에 맞춘 복수형이라 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C도 시제는 자연스럽지만 복수형 'have'를 써서 같은 오류가 있다. B는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The collection." The long phrase "of recordings ... as children" only modifies that subject. So the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes D correct. A is in the present tense, but it is plural. It agrees with nearby nouns like "recordings," "whistlers," or "shepherds" instead of the real subject. C has a reasonable tense, but its plural "have" creates the same agreement error. B is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb, so the sentence is incomplete.
g.design: The singular head noun is followed by a long modifier that contains several plural nouns, and the blank sits right after them. Students have to find the real subject and also pick a main verb rather than a participle. Two wrong answers have a plausible tense but the wrong number, and the third looks like a natural continuation of the phrase.

g.passage: Since the Halvorsen Library opened in 2019, its most photographed feature has been a pair of cantilevered reading rooms. These glass-walled rooms, which architect Ines Varga suspended above a sunken courtyard so that patrons appear to float among the birch trees below, ______ many critics who had once dismissed her earlier work as cold and austere.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'These glass-walled rooms'이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 관계절 뒤에 본동사가 필요하다. A의 'have won over'는 복수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사이며, 'Since ... 2019'라는 문맥과도 현재완료 시제로 맞는다. B는 시제는 맞지만 단수형이라, 동사 바로 앞의 'courtyard'나 'trees'와 혼동한 오답이다. C는 분사이고 D는 관계절을 하나 더 만들기 때문에, 둘 다 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "These glass-walled rooms," and after the long relative clause set off by commas, the sentence still needs a main verb. Choice A, "have won over," is a finite verb that agrees with the plural subject, and its present perfect tense fits the "Since ... 2019" context. Choice B has the right tense but is singular, so it falls for the nearby nouns "courtyard" or "trees." Choice C is a participle, and Choice D adds another relative clause, so both leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 삽입 관계절 때문에 주어와 동사가 멀리 떨어져 있어서, 수 일치(B와 비교)와 본동사 여부(C, D와 비교)를 함께 판단해야 한다.

g.passage: Painter Kofi Asante-Boateng spent a decade returning to Ghana's coast to study its fishing communities. The series of more than forty watercolors that he completed during annual visits to the town of Elmina ______ the slogans painted on the wooden canoes in meticulous detail, a feature that critics have singled out as the work's greatest strength.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 관계절과 전치사구(of more than forty watercolors, that he completed during annual visits) 때문에 단수 주어 series가 동사에서 멀어지도록 했다. 복수 명사에 끌린 오답 2개와 정동사가 없는 분사 오답 1개를 두었다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The series'이며, 'of more than forty watercolors'와 관계절 'that he completed during annual visits to the town of Elmina'는 이를 수식하는 말이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수형 정동사가 필요하므로 B(captures)가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사라는 점은 맞지만, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 watercolors나 visits에 수를 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 주절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The series." Both "of more than forty watercolors" and the relative clause "that he completed during annual visits to the town of Elmina" only describe that subject. That means the blank needs a singular finite verb, so B ("captures") is correct. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that agree with the nearby plural nouns "watercolors" or "visits" rather than with the actual subject. C is a participle, which would leave the main clause without a finite verb, so the sentence would be incomplete.

g.passage: Astronomers studying the young star system HL Tauri have long been puzzled by the dark gaps in its dusty disk. A team using radio observations now argues that the gaps, which appear as concentric rings separating bands of bright dust, ______ by still-forming planets that sweep up material as they orbit the star.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 'the gaps'에 대한 정동사 자리이다. 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입된 관계절(which ... bright dust)을 걷어내면 주어가 복수형 'gaps'이므로 복수 동사 'are carved'가 필요하다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 수동태 형태는 맞지만 단수 동사여서 삽입절 속 'dust'나 'band'에 잘못 맞춘 것이다. B와 D는 분사 형태라 that절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs the main verb of the that-clause, whose subject is "the gaps." If you set aside the interrupting relative clause ("which appear ... bright dust"), you can see that the subject is plural, so it needs the plural verb "are carved." That makes C correct. A uses the right passive form, but its verb is singular, so it wrongly agrees with a nearby noun such as "dust." B and D are participles, not finite verbs, so with either one the that-clause would have no main verb at all.
g.design: 긴 관계절 삽입 뒤의 주어-동사 일치와 정동사/분사 구분을 결합해, 두 단계를 거쳐 판단하도록 했다.

g.passage: Behavioral economists studying retirement savings have documented a striking tendency among newly hired employees. The pattern of postponing enrollment decisions, which is especially common among workers who face complicated plan menus listing dozens of fund options, ______ that an abundance of choices can discourage people from acting in their own long-term financial interest.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The pattern'이다. 'of postponing enrollment decisions'와 관계절 'which is ... fund options'는 주어를 꾸미는 삽입 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하므로 D 'suggests'가 정답이다. A와 B는 정동사이고 시제도 가능하지만, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'workers'나 'options'에 수를 맞춘 복수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C 'suggesting'은 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The pattern." The phrase "of postponing enrollment decisions" and the clause "which is ... fund options" only modify that subject. The blank therefore needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, so D, "suggests," is correct. A and B are finite verbs with acceptable tenses, but both are plural. They wrongly agree with nearby plural nouns such as "workers" or "options." C, "suggesting," is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb.
